key_facts: UPDATED Thu Sep 3 (T+1d to res=2026-09-04; DAY 3 OF SEPT 1-5 QUALIFYING WINDOW; local Straits Times Sep 2-3 + Exa CNA/Malay Mail/The Star/BBC through Sep 3 9:57 PM MYT; SUBMITTED Malaysia 0.68->0.72 [+0.04], Indonesia 0.28->0.23 [-0.05], Philippines 0.01->0.02 [+0.01], Brunei 0.02, Singapore 0.01; sum=1.00): Still NO formal state of emergency declared as of Sep 3 night, leaving Sep 4-5 as the decisive trigger window. (1) MALAYSIA (0.72): Sarawak air quality deteriorated again on Thu Sep 3 afternoon — Serian jumped from 325 midday to 391 (hazardous) at 5 PM, with Kuching 285, Sri Aman 275, Samarahan 274, Sarikei 206, and 14 areas unhealthy across Sarawak/Sabah/Labuan/Selangor; Sarawak launched 3-day RMAF C-130 cloud seeding on Sep 3 focused on hydro dams (Batang Ai/Bakun/Murum), but meteorologists warned weak winds/dry clouds prevent guaranteed rain. Crucially, CNA Sep 3 quoted Sarawak Governor Wan Junaidi Tuanku Jaafar warning API could hit 800, reiterating Malaysia statutory API >500 local haze state of emergency trigger (matching criteria wording covering a specific area within a country), alongside Deputy Premier Douglas Uggah Embas and Sabah JPBN Chairman Zainudin Aman. Malaysia is the ONLY country where top officials are actively invoking a formal state of emergency threshold in Sep 1-3 coverage. (2) INDONESIA (0.23): BBC Sep 3 reported >50,000 respiratory infections Jul-Aug (>12,000 children under 5) and ASMC Sep 2 detected 795 hotspots in Kalimantan + 144 in Sumatra, yet ZERO Sep 2-3 reporting indicates Jakarta/Prabowo preparing a national state of emergency. (3) PHILIPPINES (0.02) bumped slightly as BBC/CNA Sep 3 highlighted smoke reaching Palawan and Metro Manila; Brunei 0.02, Singapore 0.01 (PSI back to moderate).
